Read lines 5 through 10 from the poem.

She was here as a seedling,
A mere child to the rest,
Young and naïve among her dark, old elders.

But now she is a guardian,
Tall and welcoming,
Gathering and shielding the children in her arms.

The poet uses personification in these lines most likely to show that the tree —

options.label: G
options.text: provides a warning about approaching danger

options.label: H
options.text: has become stronger as it has matured

options.label: J
options.text: prevents smaller plants from having room to grow
